Subject: Pipeline hygiene sprint: updated Commit/Best Case rules + onboarding session

Team —

Quick heads-up: Revenue Ops + Sales leadership ran a short calibration last week and we made two pragmatic changes to how we classify Commit vs Best Case for FY27 pipeline hygiene. The goal is to reduce commit churn and make weekly commits actionable for finance planning.

Summary (attached PDF + checklist in Drive):
- Commit = opportunities with signed LOI/contract OR an explicit procurement date + single decision sponsor and active SOW negotiation.
- Best Case = strong intent + pricing approved by buyer but outstanding legal or procurement steps (probability lower than Commit).
- Pipeline (stage) labels remain the same, but we’re adding two required fields on any Commit: procurement owner + expected sign date (ISO).

Ask: please update any Deals currently in Commit that don’t have procurement owner or sign date by EOD Monday. RevOps will auto-send a reminder for deals flagged as “missing-commit-metadata.”

We’re running a 40-minute onboarding office hours tomorrow to walk through: rationale, examples, and walkthrough of the checklist in Salesforce/HubSpot. Attendance expected from managers and reps owning $250k+ ACV deals.

Session details:
- When: Fri 2027-04-23 10:00–10:40 PT
- Where: Zoom (link in Drive folder)
- Prep: skim the attached PDF and open the checklist spreadsheet, bring 2 example deals you’d classify as Commit today

I’ll follow with a short FAQ doc and a one-pager for CSMs.

Thanks —
Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Karthik — great questions. Short answers:

1) If legal review has started but you can’t identify a procurement owner after one outreach attempt, move to Best Case. We want Commit to mean high confidence in both budget and procurement path.
2) Month-level sign dates are acceptable for now; please include the first business day of the month in the sign_date field if buyer can only commit to month. RevOps will normalize for forecast exports.

Also note: we will automatically downgrade any deal sitting in Commit for >60 days without updated procurement metadata — that will be our guardrail to reduce commit noise.

See you at office hours. Bring those two example deals.

Evelyn
